title: Working Out the Premium Returned When Coverage under the Belrose Jewelry Protection and Care Plans Is Given Up
content:
**Scope.** This note works out what is returned to a customer who gives up live coverage under the Belrose Jewelry Protection and Care Plans.

**1. What is returned.** What is returned when live coverage is given up is the premium the customer has paid toward the plan, taken in proportion to the whole months of the term still to run, less the coverage's administration fee.

**2. The premium paid toward the plan.** The premium the customer has paid toward the plan is the premium entries booked to it, net of the give-backs booked against them.

**3. The months still to run.** The whole months still to run are the coverage's term in months less the whole months since the plan was bought and less the month in progress. The whole months since the plan was bought are counted to the handling date.

**4. The proportion.** The proportion of the premium in question is the one the whole months still to run bear to the coverage's term in months.

**5. The claim and its work order.** The work order the coverage keeps answering for is the one carrying the reference of the claim last entered against the plan.

**6. How much of the unused premium comes back.** The whole of that unused premium is returned.

**7. Order and rounding.** The share of the unused premium is worked out on the premium already reduced in proportion to the months still to run, and the administration fee is taken off only after that share has been applied. The figure is rounded to two decimal places once at the end, and nothing below zero is ever returned.

## Worked on hypothetical inputs

A plan whose term is 36 months was bought 11 whole months before the handling date, so the months still to run are 36 less 11 less the month in progress, being 24, and the proportion is 24 months of a term of 36. The premium entries booked to the plan come to 1200.00 USD with no give-backs booked against them, so the premium taken in that proportion is 800.00 USD. The whole of that unused premium is returned. The coverage's administration fee of 25.00 USD is taken off only after that, leaving 775.00 USD once the figure is rounded to two decimal places at the end. That is what comes back to the customer.
